newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF to submit 'Big Bang' bills next year.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF to submit 'Big Bang' bills next year.

text.p: The Japanese government aims to submit bills on various securities laws to the next regular session of parliament, including a new law to revitalise markets, to help realise Japan's "Big Bang" reforms, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters on Friday.

Mitsuzuka said he told a cabinet ministers' meeting on Friday that the Finance Ministry would cooperate with other ministries to raise the level of market infrastructure in Japan to international standards through the new law.
The new law will be known as the special law to revitalise markets.
He said MOF wants to submit the bills to the next regular session of parliament, which is due to begin next January.
The new law will include measures such as new trust funds and ways to increase credit liquidity, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official told the same news conference.

MOF will also cooperate with other ministries to make revisions to laws such as the securities transaction law and related laws which will include the introduction of stock options and new corporate bonds to cater to market needs, Mitsuzuka said.

The finance minister said he realised the ruling Liberal Democratic Party and other parties allied with it were considering various measures concerning the issue. But he said the government would draft the new law in the way it saw as appropriate and if necessary would coordinate with the LDP.
